--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.small_world_omega()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Compute the small-world coefficient omega. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.small_world_omega()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Compute the small-world coefficient omega. title: >- [Graph.small_world_omega()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Compute the small-world coefficient omega. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the small-world coefficient omega. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L43188-L43312){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.small_world_omega( iterations=5, nrand=10, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Small-world coefficient omega](../assets/graphs/small-world-omega.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="An eight-node ring with four chords that close four triangles. The random references average a path length L_r of 1.689 against the graph's 1.643, and the best lattice reference clusters no more than the graph itself, C_l = C = 0.667. The card computes 1.689 / 1.643 minus 0.667 / 0.667, omega = 0.028: near 0, the small-world middle between a lattice (-1) and a random graph (1)." width="100%"} Telesford et al. (2011) compare a network both with a random graph and with a lattice: $$\omega = \frac{L_r}{L} - \frac{C}{C_\ell},$$ where $L$ is the average shortest path length, $C$ the average clustering coefficient, $L_r$ the average path length of random references and $C_\ell$ the best clustering of lattice references (see `random_reference()` and `lattice_reference()`). Omega lies roughly between -1 and 1: near 0 means small-world, near -1 lattice-like, and near 1 random-like, which places a network on the order-to-randomness spectrum in a way that sigma does not. The graph must be undirected and connected, and is treated as simple. The result is random; use `seed=` for reproducible values. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [iterations]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[5]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Rewiring rounds for the lattice references (the random references use twice as many), default 5 as in NetworkX. [nrand]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of reference pairs (default 10). [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The coefficient omega. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or disconnected, or has fewer than four nodes or two edges. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Follows NetworkX's `omega` ($C_\ell$ is the largest clustering among the lattice references and the original graph). The lattice references use the corrected swap criterion described in `lattice_reference()`. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~small_world_sigma`) : Compare clustering and path length with random references. [](`~lattice_reference`) : The lattice-like graphs that omega compares against. [](`~random_reference`) : The random graphs that omega compares against. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Omega is near -1 for a lattice, near 0 for a small world and near 1 for a random graph: ::: {#fdc9578e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_smallworld_graph(n=60, k=6, p=0.2, seed=1) round(graph.small_world_omega(seed=1), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.02 ``` ::: ::: ### Between order and chance Rewiring a ring lattice a little at a time moves omega from the lattice end toward the random end, crossing 0 with about a fifth of the edges rewired. Unlike `small_world_sigma()`, which rates the plain ring highly, omega places it near the lattice end: ::: {#a8c10481 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl rings = { p: ec.Graph().add_smallworld_graph(n=60, k=6, p=p, seed=1) for p in [0.0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0] } pl.DataFrame({ "p": list(rings), "sigma": [g.small_world_sigma(seed=1) for g in rings.values()], "omega": [g.small_world_omega(seed=1) for g in rings.values()], }) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
